summary: Berlevåg Airport (BVG) is a small regional airport serving the remote coastal municipality of Berlevåg in Finnmark, northern Norway, situated well above the Arctic Circle. Operated by Avinor, it provides a vital lifeline for the local fishing community and is one of the most northerly airports in mainland Norway. The short runway and exposed coastal location make it notable for weather-sensitive operations typical of STOL airports in the far north.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly to Berlevåg Airport?
A: Widerøe is the primary airline serving Berlevåg, operating turboprop flights primarily to Tromsø and other regional Norwegian destinations.

Q: How far is the airport from Berlevåg town center?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometers from the town center, with a short drive typical of the area's compact layout.

Q: When is the best time to visit Berlevåg?
A: Summer (June–August) offers the midnight sun and milder weather, while winter brings the polar night and opportunities to see the northern lights.

Q: Are there facilities at the airport?
A: As a small regional airport, facilities are limited but include a basic terminal with essential services for travelers.
transport_tips: Ground transport options at Berlevåg are limited due to the airport's remote location, so arrange a taxi or pre-booked transfer in advance. Rental cars are scarce in the area, so coordinate with local providers before arrival. Many visitors and locals rely on arranged pickups from the few local drivers familiar with the region.
local_tip: Pack layers and windproof clothing regardless of season—the exposed coastal location means conditions can change rapidly, and even summer temperatures can feel cold when the wind picks up off the Barents Sea.
